provenance: Manual transcription of physical TT-NN inverse, hidden-state and serial localhost HTTP observations; bounded examples, not a corpus-scale accuracy or fleet performance study.
hardware: Two physical Blackhole P150a cards: Clef 27B on PCIe IDs 0+1 (1x2), Clef-Flash 9B on ID 0 (1x1). Firmware 19.11.0.0, TT-KMD 2.10.0, TT-Metal 0.77.0. All probe meshes shut down and ports 8189/8190 released.

packages.build: nix build --no-link --print-out-paths .#qwen38 --option substituters '' --option builders '' succeeded, including device-free installCheck

change: Horner lower-triangular inverse keeps its existing R tensor as output_tensor of each add after the preceding matmul has finished reading R. The same 30 matmuls and arithmetic order remain; R has the same shape, FP32 dtype and memory configuration throughout. Per inverse, Python-level TT-NN output arguments change from 31 newly allocated add outputs to one newly allocated add output plus 30 reuse calls; matmul outputs remain 30 allocations. Reuse is local to one solve, never cached across calls or device traces. The separately probed optional_output_tensor matmul reuse was not retained.
method: Physical TT-NN 0.77. An in-memory-only selector compiled original and candidate inverses from the same installed source; no baseline branch was packaged. Full inverse and hidden tensors were first compared elementwise with torch.equal. A separate strict probe reinterpreted contiguous FP32/BF16 host tensors as uint8 and asserted zero byte mismatches for the retained reuse_add path on both physical meshes. Warm serial HTTP A/B excluded first-use compilation and hidden-capture overhead; four long and three short 27B cycles each ran baseline, reuse_add, reuse_both, reuse_both, reuse_add, baseline. Flash used four baseline, reuse_add, reuse_add, baseline cycles per shape. HTTP results include parsing, device execution and the released head; response probabilities are rounded by that head.

long_1342_tokens.result: No demonstrated long-request Flash gain; medians differ by 0.0066 seconds within host-load variation.

limits: The 27B HTTP speedup is an in-process matched warm comparison of these two text shapes; the separately rebuilt process ran under different host load and its raw times are not cross-process speedup evidence. The Flash 1342-token comparison showed no gain. First requests in fresh rebuilt processes compiled kernels (27B short 72 s, long 53 s; Flash short 39 s, long 50 s); no cold-start improvement is claimed. Exact numerical equality is for the recorded tensors and requests, not a corpus-wide accuracy guarantee or an admission decision.
